resources.instruction: High-risk task: besides the normal review, check security by STRIDE on the code you read. Spoofing (which endpoint lacks authentication, passwords hashed with a weak algorithm, tokens that never expire or are not checked on the server); Tampering (input not checked for type, length, format; string concatenation into SQL; the wrong HTTP method for a write); Repudiation (no log for sign-in, authorization failures, data changes; logs containing passwords or tokens); Information disclosure (stack traces, internal IDs, secrets in code, responses returning extra fields); Denial of service (lists without pagination, no size or time limits, regexes that can blow up); Elevation of privilege (permission checked only on the UI side, one user reaching another's resource by ID). Record only findings with file:line and the exploitation scenario; for something already protected at another layer, say which layer.

Attach each security finding to an OWASP category when reasonable, so the reviewer can assess it easily: A01 broken access control (missing permission check, IDOR, wide CORS, path traversal); A02 cryptographic failures (weak hashing, plain storage, no TLS); A03 injection (SQL, OS command, template); A04 insecure design (business logic flaws, no thought of abuse); A05 security misconfiguration (default passwords, detailed error pages); A06 vulnerable components (an old version with a CVE); A07 authentication failures; A08 data integrity failures (untrusted deserialization); A09 missing security logging; A10 SSRF (a user-supplied URL). When reporting, hide secret values: write the variable name or the location, do not copy the real value.
